ballot_text.source_title: State Issue 1 - The Neighborhood Safety, Drug Treatment, and Rehabilitation Amendment (the memo links the SOS page as 'Issue 1-To Reduce Penalties for Crimes of Obtaining, Possessing, and Using Illegal Drugs', which is our title)
ballot_text.type_quote: the language of the 2018 ballot initiative, State Issue 1, and consider potential impact of its provisions

fact.quote: On July 23, 3018, the ballot initiative was certified by the Secretary of State for the November 6, 2018, election, appearing as State Issue 1.
fact.why: WEAK inference, not stated. Type: the title says 'Amendment', the memo calls it a ballot initiative and speaks of 'the rigid nature of a constitutional amendment'. Fact: the memo records the Ballot Board's action as finding the petition compliant with the single subject rule (December 12, 2017) and records one certification, as 'State Issue 1' (the source's 'July 23, 3018' is its own typo); it never mentions art. II sec. 1e(B) or a second question. A (B)(2) finding would have produced two questions. The Ballot Board's own records (ohiosos.gov) were refused, so this rests on a secondary summary; D3 may prefer to treat it as null.

threshold.rule: majority of the electors voting thereon
threshold.quote: Any proposed law or amendment to the constitution submitted to the electors as provided in 1a and 1b, if approved by a majority of the electors voting thereon, shall take effect thirty days after the election at which it was approved and shall be published by the secretary of state.
threshold.matched: by the type the ballot text shows [inferred] (amendment; data/measure/ballot-texts.json); the ballot text shows it is not an initiated amendment the ballot board finds to conflict with art. II sec. 1e(B)(1) (put as two questions) [inferred] (data/measure/ballot-texts.json); proposed by the initiative [stated: the ballot text read, data/measure/ballot-texts.json], so Ohio Const. art. II, sec. 1b governs (initiated statute and initiated constitutional amendment)
